chapter: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
title: Vinson invites him to join his new band
summary: Gus met Vinson at the Savoy with Cootie; after the Army Vinson asked him to join his own band, which he did in 1946.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, anyway, -- yeah, that's right, Cootie got him out of that band. And so when you met him at the Savoy, was he playing in Cootie's band?
Eddie Vinson?
Eddie Vinson.
Oh, yeah, he was playing and singing. Yes.
But when he first went, he was so shy and he nearly ran away and ran back home.
Who? Eddie was shy?
(Laughter.)
Cootie said he'd nearly had to handcuff him to keep him --
He could have been, he could have been.
Because he was from out of Texas and he never thought about going to New York.
Well, --
And Cootie sent him the fare and he didn't come and -- so when you met him, he must have found his feet by then.
Well, yes, he'd been playing with Cootie.
Yeah, he was -- got himself at home.

He told me, when I got out of the Army, when I saw him, he said he was going to start his own band. And he wanted me to play with him. So I said, okay. But I didn't know how long for sure that would be.
Yeah.
But when he started his band, he called
me.
This was in New York?
This was in New York.
And you joined him there.
I joined him, yeah.
I wonder what year -- it was about '45 or '46? '46, maybe?
'45 or '46, yeah. Yeah, about '46.
